uncertain_sources: The lecture suppresses the phase-space cell in the classical ideal-gas integral; the chapter restores h to the power 3N so that the partition function is dimensionless and notes that this beta-independent factor does not alter the mean-energy derivative.

The lecture says the factor one over N factorial is immaterial in the classical calculation; the chapter preserves that fixed-N energy statement while qualifying that indistinguishability is essential for absolute entropy, extensivity, and particle-number variations.
The ideal-gas entropy is assigned as an exercise; the chapter supplies the standard large-N result as the direct completion of S equals beta E plus log Z.

The finite-height gravitational integral is started and then set aside before the infinite-atmosphere simplification; the chapter evaluates the finite integral and its mean potential energy as the minimal completion of the displayed setup.
The final fluctuation formula is promised but deferred; the chapter states the second-derivative variance and heat-capacity identities that the lecture explicitly previews.
